The planning-specific hard requirements are met: structural typed-error acceptance at line 117, declarative public `repair_target_paths` with same-input subset assertion at line 125, and the settled test-support activation mechanism at line 135.

## Technical soundness and architectural fit

The revised S1.d explicitly covers the prior journal-free control-cleanup gap at line 151 without changing journal recovery semantics.

## Decomposition and dependencies

The five-story graph and leaf wiring rule at lines 44–67 and 141–178 correctly sequence S1/S3 in parallel, S2/S4 after S1, and S5 after all prerequisites. Tasks have clear ownership and test approaches.

## Risks and actionability

Material risks are recorded with mitigations at lines 209–215. Each critical task specifies implementation boundaries, acceptance behavior, and relevant tests.

## Prior review feedback

The prior F1 is addressed by S1.d’s control-only teardown design (line 151). Prior F2 is addressed according to the issue’s settled owner decision and explicit self-dev-dependency design (line 135).
